sentences.text: The name Datousaurus translates to "chieftain lizard" or "big-head lizard," a pun based on its large head.
This herbivorous dinosaur measured approximately 10 to 13.9 meters in length.
It possessed a deep and large skull, a feature unusual for sauropods.
Only two partial skeletons of this animal have been discovered to date.
Neither of these partial skeletons included an articulated skull, though one skull attributed to the genus has been found.
The genus was named by Dong Zhiming and Tang Zilu in 1984.
Fossils were discovered in the lower Shaximiao Formation at Dashanpu in Zigong, Sichuan province, China.
Elongated vertebrae allowed it to reach higher, while its teeth were spoon-shaped.
Researchers suggest that the different feeding adaptations of Datousaurus and Shunosaurus may indicate they ate different plants or fed at different heights to reduce competition.
The rarity of Datousaurus fossils suggests it may not have lived in herds like other sauropods.
Datousaurus is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae.
The parent group of the genus is Eusauropoda.
Datousaurus lived approximately 168 to 162 million years ago during the Bathonian and Callovian stages.
It lived in the Middle Jurassic alongside sauropods like Shunosaurus and Omeisaurus, the neornithischian Xiaosaurus, the stegosaur Huayangosaurus, and the carnivore Gasosaurus.
